  1 I.      IDENTIFICATION


 2    Q.        PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME AND BUSINESS ADDRESS FOR THE RECORD.

 3         A.     My name is Larry Blank. My business address is TAHOEconomics, LLC, 6061

 4                Montgomery       Road,    Midlothian,     TX     76065.     My     email    address   is

 5                LB@tahoeconomics.com.

 6    Q.        DID YOU PREPARE DIRECT TESTIMONY IN THIS CASE THAT WAS FILED

 7              MAY 1, 2026?

 8         A.     Yes.

 9    Q.        IS YOUR DIRECT TESTIMONY RELEVANT TO THIS PHASE OF THIS

10              CASE?

11         A.     Yes, my Direct Testimony filed May 1, 2026, in its entirety, is relevant to the

12                Commission’s consideration of the Comprehensive Stipulation (“Stipulation”) filed on

13                June 22, 2026, and the testimony filed in support of the Stipulation filed on June 30,

14                2026.

15    Q.        ON WHOSE BEHALF ARE YOU TESTIFYING?

16         A.     I am testifying on behalf of the Utility Division Staff (“Staff”) of the New Mexico

17                Public Regulation Commission (“Commission” or “PRC”).


18 II.     PURPOSE


19    Q.        WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR OPPOSITION TESTIMONY?

20         A.     I address certain deficiencies in the “Comprehensive Stipulation” filed by

21                Southwestern Public Service Company (“SPS” or “Company”) and supported by

22                certain parties. Specifically, I address the following within the Stipulation:


      Opposition Testimony of Larry Blank         Case No. 25-00079-UT                             Page 3
 1                 [1.1 of the Stipulation] The Stipulation is silent on my recommendation for

2          consistency in the 12-CP values used in the Texas-New Mexico jurisdictional allocation in

3          which the Texas jurisdiction restrains SPS to utilize historical 12-CP values adjusted for

4          known and measurable changes. Deviation from this approach in New Mexico by allowing

5          forecasted 12-CP values creates an inconsistency in allocation methodology and an

6          opportunity for SPS to over-forecast to New Mexico and cause a double-recovery of

7          revenue requirement in the Texas and New Mexico jurisdictions.

8                 [1.3 of the Stipulation] Although the parties to the Stipulation have adopted my

9          recommendation to remove the accredited capacity of the Cunningham BESS from the

10         New Mexico 12-CP measures used to compute the 12-CP jurisdiction allocation ratios

11         between New Mexico, Texas, and FERC, the application of this in the Stipulation is flawed

12         in that they have removed planning reserve margin (“PRM”) from the accredited capacity

13         value. This PRM adjustment made by SPS and the stipulating parties is not accurate

14         because resource adequacy requirements are not solely met by rate base items, and not all

15         rate base capacity serves resource adequacy. The full amount of the Cunningham BESS

16         accredited capacity will be used to satisfy the Southwest Power Pool (“SPP”) resource

17         adequacy requirements, and the full amount is an offset to the total load requirements in

18         New Mexico including PRM. Because the Stipulation raises PRM and resource adequacy,

19         the proper way to do that would be to determine the total generation capacity in the SPP

20         Rate Base (including both New Mexico and Texas) used to meet resource adequacy

21         requirements and then determine what percent of that is the Cunningham BESS. The New

22         Mexico 12 CP values could then be reduced by that amount. The Stipulation’s PRM

23         adjustment is misguided in a way that acts as though the BESS is scheduled independently




     Opposition Testimony of Larry Blank      Case No. 25-00079-UT                            Page 4
  1             to meet resource adequacy requirements and this is not accurate. The purpose of this

 2             calculation is the development of an allocator for generation capacity in the rate base, not

 3             all resource adequacy beyond the rate base, and New Mexico’s share of that is reduced by

 4             the full amount of the accredited BESS capacity.

 5                     [1.11 of the Stipulation] The total amounts shown in Stipulation Exhibit A are

 6             inconsistent with Staff’s recommendations due to the difference between Staff’s

 7             recommended revenue requirement and that in the Stipulation. I provide the revenue

 8             allocations utilizing Staff’s recommended revenue requirement.

 9                     [1.12 of the Stipulation] Although Staff is not opposed to the Stipulation’s

10             provisions related to the Electric Affordability Program, the Stipulation is silent regarding

11             the initial benefit threshold and Staff’s recommendation that it initially be set at 5%.

12                     [1.13 of the Stipulation] Although Staff is not opposed to the changes and

13             implementation of demand ratchets, the new demand ratchet for primary service customers

14             should be phased in over a period of eleven months as provided in my Direct Testimony.


15                      III.   SUMMARY OF OPPOSITION TO STIPULATION

16   Q.        PLEASE SUMMARIZE YOUR OPPOSITION POINTS AND REFERENCE THE

17             RELEVANT SECTIONS OF YOUR DIRECT TESTIMONY ALREADY FILED.

18        A.        The following summarizes my review and recommendations in opposition to the

19                  Stipulation.

20             1.      Jurisdictional Allocation Mismatch. The Stipulation is silent on the SPS-

21                     proposed jurisdictional allocation used to separate the revenue requirement

22                     between the Texas, New Mexico, and Federal Energy Regulatory Commission

23                     (“FERC”) jurisdictions, which utilizes forecasted 12-CP and energy allocation



     Opposition Testimony of Larry Blank            Case No. 25-00079-UT                              Page 5
  1                       ratios. This methodology is not used in those other jurisdictions, which creates a

 2                       mismatch that causes the potential for over- or under-recovery of revenue

 3                       requirement. In this case, because SPS has forecasted much more load growth in

 4                       New Mexico than in Texas, and the fact that Texas does not allow forecasted test

 5                       years, there will be some double recovery of revenue requirement if these different

 6                       methods are applied. Texas requires the use of actual historical data and allows

 7                       adjustments for known and measurable changes but does not allow forecasts. My

 8                       recommendation, solely for the purpose of the jurisdictional separations, is to use

 9                       what is required and allowed in Texas. This will maintain consistency on this

10                       important matter to avoid over- or under-recovery of revenue requirement. See pp.

11                       7-10 of Larry Blank Direct Testimony, filed May 1, 2026.

12

13              2.       Stipulation 12-CP Adjustment for Cunningham BESS. Although the parties to

14                       the Stipulation have adopted my recommendation to remove the accredited capacity

15                       of the Cunningham BESS from the New Mexico 12-CP measures used to compute

16                       the 12-CP jurisdiction allocation ratios between New Mexico, Texas, and FERC,

17                       the application of this in the Stipulation is flawed in that they have removed

18                       planning reserve margin (“PRM”) from the accredited capacity value.                        It is

19                       imperative that when any capacity and/or energy facility costs are directly assigned

20                       to New Mexico that there be an offsetting credit in the jurisdictional allocation. The

21                       Cunningham BESS only provides capacity value, but no energy value. 1 Therefore,

22                       I am recommending an offsetting adjustment to the New Mexico 12-CPs equal to



     1
         If there was energy value, we would need to determine the offsetting energy cost benefit to New Mexico.


     Opposition Testimony of Larry Blank                 Case No. 25-00079-UT                                      Page 6
  1                the expected accredited capacity of the storage system. This reduces the amount of

 2                the remaining capacity costs that need to be allocated to New Mexico. See pp. 10-

 3                14 of Larry Blank Direct Testimony, filed May 1, 2026. The PRM adjustment

 4                used by the stipulating parties is improper and should be denied. Because the

 5                Stipulation raises PRM and resource adequacy, the proper way to do that would be

 6                to determine the total generation capacity in the SPP Rate Base (including both

 7                New Mexico and Texas) used to meet resource adequacy requirements and then

 8                determine what percent of that is the Cunningham BESS. The New Mexico 12 CP

 9                values could then be reduced by that amount. The Stipulation PRM adjustment is

10                misguided in a way that acts as though the BESS is scheduled independently from

11                the remainder of the system and this is not accurate. The purpose of this calculation

12                is the development of an allocator for generation capacity in the rate base, not all

13                resource adequacy beyond the rate base, and New Mexico’s share of that is reduced

14                by the full amount of the accredited BESS capacity.

15

16         3.     Banding and Exhibit A to the Stipulation. The level of revenue requirement

17                increase recommended by Staff is much lower than that proposed by SPS and much

18                lower than the Stipulation revenue requirement. This allows more latitude or

19                bandwidth in the distribution of the revenue increase across customer classes. I

20                recommend that no rate class receive an increase less than 50% of the Staff’s system

21                average base rate revenue increase. I recommend that the above-cost revenue from

22                those rate classes be set at 50% of the system average and be allocated to the other

23                rate classes in proportion to the cost-based increases of those classes.        This




     Opposition Testimony of Larry Blank      Case No. 25-00079-UT                              Page 7
  1                establishes Staff’s proposed banding in which no customer class receives less than

 2                50% of system average, and most of the other classes, including residential, range

 3                between 150% to 200% of system average. Only one rate class, Secondary General

 4                Service, would receive an increase at cost of service. Therefore, this should clarify

 5                Staff’s opposition to Exhibit A of the Stipulation, which should be denied in favor

 6                of the results found in my Direct Testimony. See pp. 14-17 of Larry Blank Direct

 7                Testimony (including Exhibit LB-2), filed May 1, 2026.

 8

 9         4.     Rate Design. I recommend limiting the service availability charge for residential

10                customers to $15.00 per month, which is a 33.9% increase over the current charge

11                of $11.20, and consistent with the percentage increase for small general service.

12                See p. 18 of Larry Blank Direct Testimony, filed May 1, 2026.

13

14         5.     Demand Ratchet Implementation. The Stipulation ignores my recommendations

15                for a new demand ratchet for primary general service and a significant change in

16                the ratchet for transmission service customers draws questions of appropriate

17                timing for implementation. As proposed, these ratchets would retroactively

18                consider the billing demands from the previous 11 months in the first month the

19                ratchet becomes effective. The Commission should consider a phase-in period of

20                11 months before the ratchets take effect. That is, in the 12th billing cycle after the

21                rates take effect, SPS will now start using the higher of the current month’s billing

22                demand or 85% of the past 11 months. See pp. 20-21 of Larry Blank Direct

23                Testimony, filed May 1, 2026.




     Opposition Testimony of Larry Blank       Case No. 25-00079-UT                               Page 8
  1

 2             6.      Electric Affordability Program.          Staff generally supports the Company’s

 3                     proposed Electric Affordability Program (“EAP”) and the additional provisions on

 4                     EAP with the Stipulation. Because this program is being implemented for the first

 5                     time, this benefit is in addition to the LIHEAP support already received by these

 6                     customers, and not knowing the revenue impact on other customers, I recommend

 7                     that the PIPP be based on five percent (5%) of household income and not the three

 8                     percent proposed by the Company.          See pp. 21-22 of Larry Blank Direct

 9                     Testimony, filed May 1, 2026.

10   Q.        DO YOU HAVE THE DATA TO DEVELOP A REVISED ADJUSTMENT TO

11             THE 12-CP JURISDICTIONAL ALLOCATION TO CONSIDER RATE BASE

12             CAPACITY SERVING RESOURCE ADEQUACY AS YOU HAVE DESCRIBED?

13        A.        No. The flawed PRM adjustment included by the stipulating parties is the first time

14                  this adjustment has been suggested in the course of case. We have not had the

15                  opportunity to conduct discovery of SPS to see if they can provide the portion of

16                  capacity in the rate base necessary to meet SPP resource adequacy. Therefore, this

17                  issue of resource adequacy and the PRM adjustment introduced by the Stipulation

18                  requires further work and is not proper for inclusion at this time.

19   Q.        PLEASE PROVIDE A SUMMARY OF STAFF’S RECOMMENDED REVENUE
